correctness.rationale: For a weight-two support (a,b), deleting one of its two ones yields weight-one output positions a and b-1: adjacent words consume one distinct weight-one descendant, separated words consume two. For any code with t adjacent and s separated supports, t+2s≤n-1. Adjacent starts cannot be consecutive because then their zero-deletion weight-two shadows collide, hence t≤floor(n/2). Thus |C|≤floor((n-1+floor(n/2))/2)=floor((3n-2)/4). The proposed even-start adjacent and mod-four spaced pairs consume disjoint weight-one descendants; their zero-deletion output pair distances and first-coordinate residue blocks prevent all weight-two collisions. The construction attains the bound for all n, including short boundary n=2,3. Independent exhaustive single-deletion shadow simulation validates n=2..45; independently computed exact compatibility-graph independence numbers for n=2..8 match the formula. Infinite conclusion comes from analytic shadow argument, not finite tests. The modified-VT color size ceil(n/2) for n≥4 is a separate residue pairing count; compare same Hamming layer.
residual_risks: Exactly one deletion and Hamming weight exactly two; distinct outputs considered as sets, not multiplicities; does not classify every maximizer.
